newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JAN 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JAN 3.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The authorities are concerned by the new form of tax evasion presented by machines that issue receipts without cataloguing inflows. The finance ministry is considering releasing the names of these tax evaders to the public next week.
--An encouraging start to 1997 at the Athens bourse yesterday, with intense foreign and local investor interest in bank shares. The general price index jumped 2.26 percent to settle at 954.54 points.
--The insurance market in Greece is lagging behind its European counterpart, according to European figures.
--The charge paid by insurance companies to the auxiliary fund will be doubled to 10 percent if the development ministry has its way, to the dissatisfaction of firms.

--There was strong demand for previous bond issues on the secondary market yesterday. Meanwhile, increased liquidity, the reduction in returns from T-bills following the levying of the new tax as well as reduced inflation is expected to lead to a new reduction in banking interest rates.

--The government is preparing to announce new incentives for employers to create 40,000 jobs. The measures will include increased subsidies for new jobs on daily wages, insurance and social security contributions.
--The state culled 400 billion drachmas yesterday on its recent treasury bill issue - the first to carry the new tax - overshooting its target of 330 billion.
--The 1996 budget is expected to close with a 200 billion drachma discrepancy, more than the 170 billion originally forecast, sources say, due primarily to the farmers' blockades.
--How to share out some 100 billion drachmas in national and European Union funds on developing small and medium size enterprises will have been decided by the end of the month.
--The special tax prosecution squad will go into operation as of end-February.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis receives an SOS from Greek shipowners based in London calling on him to take immediate measures to improve the competitiveness of Greek shipping.
